implementation_notes: TypeScript's `baseUrl`/`paths` aliases exist to hide `../../../`, and they routinely grow into a routing layer that makes the module graph illegible: a feature can import anything by naming a top-level folder, and nothing constrains the direction. Diagnosis is `madge` with the alias map, or the IDE's reference graph. Consolidation is to make each feature a directory with an `index.ts` that exports its public surface and forbid importing across features except through those surfaces — enforced with ESLint's `no-restricted-imports`, which is the only thing that will actually hold the line.
idiom_name: path aliases so deep that the import graph is unreadable
pitfalls: `paths` aliases let a deep import bypass the package's `index.ts`, so a broken internal file becomes part of the public API.
`any`-typed module boundaries mean the compiler cannot tell you that a 'feature' module imports another feature's internals.
Barrel files plus aliases together give you a dependency graph that neither the compiler nor a grep can reconstruct.
